title: Emergent Dissipation from Fluctuating Quantum-Network Topology
abstract: We investigate how dissipation can emerge in a quantum network from temporal fluctuations of the interaction   topology. For a network whose graph is redrawn at short time intervals, the averaged   dynamics yields a Markovian master equation: the mean network fixes the   coherent part and the covariance fixes the dissipative structure. The   covariance eigenvalues set the noise strengths, while its eigenvectors   determine the collective operators on which those strengths act. Two ensembles   with identical mean adjacency and covariance spectra but different   eigenvectors produce distinct dynamics despite identical purity. A physically   realizable model yields an analytically predicted dissipative gap, giving   quasi-protected dynamics. These results establish fluctuating connectivity as   a resource for engineering quantum dissipation and protection.
summary: This theoretical work analyzes how quantum dissipation arises in a network whose connections fluctuate randomly over time. It shows that the resulting dynamics are determined not just by the average connectivity, but critically by the specific structure (eigenvectors) of the connectivity fluctuations. This establishes fluctuating connectivity as a controllable resource for quantum engineering.
main_problem: The paper investigates how quantum dissipation can emerge in a quantum network due to the temporal fluctuations of its interaction topology.
main_result: The dynamics are governed by both the mean topology (coherent part) and the covariance structure (dissipative part), showing that identical mean spectra do not guarantee identical dynamics.
method: The analysis derives an effective Lindblad master equation using a rapid-switching expansion of the random-unitary channel, followed by spectral decomposition of the covariance matrix.
model_or_system: The system is an N-site quantum network of two-level systems whose interaction edges fluctuate randomly over short time intervals. The dynamics are modeled via a topology-averaged master equation.
key_observables: Fidelity, Purity, Sector-resolved Coherence, and the Dissipative Gap ($\gamma_{	ext{gap}}$).
important_parameters: The time step ($\Delta t$), the correlation parameter ($\kappa$), and the structure of the covariance matrix eigenvalues/eigenvectors.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the leading-order generator expansion for small time steps ($\Delta t$), and specific comparisons are made between global and community correlation ensembles.
figures_summary: The notes describe comparisons of coherence decay rates and purity calculations for different correlation ensembles, and the identification of a slow decay mode ($\gamma_{	ext{slow}}$) matching the gap.
paper_structure: The paper builds from deriving the effective generator via expansion, separating the roles of the mean Hamiltonian and the covariance matrix, and then comparing specific correlated ensembles (global vs. community) to demonstrate non-equivalence of dynamics.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous framework for understanding how environmental coupling, modeled by fluctuating connectivity, generates dissipation, offering tools to engineer dissipation or protect quantum information.
